(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He was born and raised in [[Istanbul]], and was selected 26th in the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Korkmaz is {{height|ft=6|in=7}} tall and plays the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. ==Early years== Korkmaz was born in [[Bakırköy]], [[Istanbul]]. He started playing basketball with the school team when he was nine. In 2012, he moved to [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]], from Efes' junior team, Yeşilyurt Spor Kulübü, for $250,000, at the age of 15. ==Professional career== ===Anadolu Efes (2013–2017)=== In his first year in the Efes club infrastructure, Korkmaz played for the junior and youth teams of Efes. He was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] for the 2013–14 season to the [[Turkish basketball league system|Turkish 2nd-tier-level]] [[Turkish Basketball First League|TB2L]] team Pertevniyal, which was at the time the [[farm team|farm club]] of [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]. In the summer of 2014, Korkmaz moved to the senior men's Anadolu Efes first team. His contract with Efes included a $2 million buyout clause for the [[NBA]].{{cite web |date=May 11, 2017 |title=Korkmaz wants to join the Sixers, his $2 m buyout keeps him in Europe |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/446680/korkmaz-wants-join-sixers-2-m-buyout-keeps-europe |access-date=August 8, 2023 |website=eurohoops.net}} On June 13, 2016, Korkmaz was one of 13 different international underclassmen to enter the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|url=http://www.sports.yahoo.com/news/combine-buzz-194205610.html|title=Combine buzz: Skal Labissiere impresses|work=Yahoo|date=May 12, 2016|access-date=May 11, 2017}} He was selected 26th in the first round, by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Seltzer|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-take-simmons-luwawu-cabarrot-korkmaz-draft|title=Sixers Take Simmons, Luwawu-Cabarrot, Korkmaz in Draft|date=June 24, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 24, 2016}} After being drafted, Korkmaz decided to return to Anadolu Efes for at least another season. ===Banvit (2016–2017)=== In December 2016, Korkmaz was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] by [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] to [[Bandırma B.İ.K.|Banvit]].{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7hkx6ifhjdhe7or7/efes-swaps-korkmaz-for-mutaf|title=Efes swaps Korkmaz for Mutaf|publisher=Euroleague.net|access-date=May 11, 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/euroleague/366771/furkan-korkmaz-loan-banvit|title=Furkan Korkmaz on loan to Banvit|publisher=Eurohoops.net|date=December 19, 2016|access-date=May 11, 2017}} In February 2017, he won the [[Turkish Basketball Cup|Turkish Cup]] with Banvit, which was the first trophy in the club's history.{{cite web|date=February 19, 2017|url=http://www.tbf.org.tr/en/detail/2017/02/19/integral-forex-turkish-cup-champion-is-banvit!|title=Integral Forex Turkish Cup Champion is Banvit!|publisher=TBF.org.tr|access-date=May 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822215838/http://www.tbf.org.tr/en/detail/2017/02/19/integral-forex-turkish-cup-champion-is-banvit!|archive-date=August 22, 2017|url-status=dead}} In the same season, Korkmaz was the inaugural winner of the [[Basketball Champions League]] (BCL) [[Basketball Champions League Best Young Player|Best Young Player]] award of the [[2016–17 Basketball Champions League|2016–17 season]] of the [[European professional club basketball system|European-wide third-tier level]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.basketballcl.com/16-17/news/star-lineup-revealed-korkmaz-named-best-young-player|title=Star Lineup revealed, Korkmaz named Best Young Player|date=April 30, 2017|access-date=January 16, 2018|publisher=Basketballcl.com}} In the BCL, he reached the championship game of the competition with Banvit, where his team lost 63–59 to [[Iberostar Tenerife]]. Korkmaz recorded 4 points and 2 rebounds in the final game.{{Cite news|url=http://www.basketballcl.com/iberostar-tenerife-crowned-inaugural-basketball-champions-league-winners|title=Iberostar Tenerife crowned inaugural Basketball Champions League winners|date=April 30, 2017|access-date=June 14, 2017|publisher=BasketballCL.com}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2017–2024)=== [[File:Furkan Korkmaz 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Korkmaz warms up with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2019]] On July 4, 2017, Korkmaz signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite news|title=Sixers sign 2016 first-round draft pick Furkan Korkmaz|url=http://global.nba.com/news/sixers-sign-2016-first-round-draft-pick-furkan-korkmaz|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2017|access-date=August 8, 2023}} During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=2017-2018 Philadelphia 76ers Knicks Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Philadelphia-Sixers/22/Transaction_History/2018|website=RealGM.com|access-date=April 15, 2018}} In Philadelphia's first game of the [[2018 NBA Summer League]], Korkmaz scored 40 points (including 8 three-pointers) in 28 minutes during an 89–95 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]]. It was the fifth-best scoring performance in Summer League history.{{cite news|first=Nick|last=Schwartz|title=Meet Furkan Korkmaz, the Sixers' Summer League phenom|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2018/07/meet-furkan-korkmaz-the-sixers-summer-league-phenom|work=For The Win|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=July 7, 2018|access-date=July 12, 2018}}{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Ellentuck|title=Sixers' Furkan Korkmaz is one of the best NBA scorers of all time! (In July)|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2018/7/6/17543232/furkan-korkmaz-sixers-summer-league-stats-legend|website=SBNation.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 12, 2018}} After not seeing much playing time, Korkmaz requested a trade from the 76ers in November 2018. However, he ultimately stayed with the team{{cite web|first=Antonis|last=Stroggylakis|title=Korkmaz: I was the first guy who asked to be traded, six players left and I stayed|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/877124/furkan-korkmaz-i-was-the-first-guy-who-asked-to-be-traded-six-seven-players-left-and-i-stayed/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=May 13, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2023}} On December 10, Korkmaz scored 18 points off the bench in a win over the [[Detroit Pistons]]. On December 12, he had his first career start in place of the injured [[Jimmy Butler]]. On July 25, 2019, Korkmaz re-signed with the 76ers on a two-year contract.{{cite web|first=Kurt|last=Gies|title=Team Re-Signs Furkan Korkmaz|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/team-re-signs-furkan-korkmaz|website=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=July 25, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski|title=Agent: Furkan Korkmaz returning to 76ers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27251037|website=ESPN.com|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=July 27, 2019}} Throughout the season, he had made his way in and out the starting lineup, playing both [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]].{{cite web|title=Furkan Korkmaz Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/korkmfu01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 10, 2024}} On November 2, Korkmaz hit the game-winner against the [[2019–20 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]]. On February 7, 2020, Korkmaz scored a career-high 34 points off the bench against the [[2019–20 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]]. One game later, Korkmaz went off again, scoring 31 points off the bench against the [[2019–20 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Furkan Korkmaz Follows Career Night With Another Huge Game As Sixers Beat Bulls|url=https://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2020/02/09/furkan-korkmaz-follows-career-night-with-another-huge-game-as-sixers-beat-bulls/|website=CBSLocal.com|date=February 9, 2020|access-date=August 8, 2023}} Korkmaz started 12 games, and averaged a career-high 21.7 minutes a game, and established career-high averages in points and rebounds per game at 9.8 and 2.3, respectively, while shooting a career-high 40.2% in three-point field goal accuracy. In the [[2020–21 NBA season|2020–21 season]], Korkmaz had 11 starts in the abbreviated season, and averaged 9.1 points per game, along with 2.1 rebounds per game and 37.5% three-point shooting. He had career highs in assists and steals per game, at 1.5 and 0.9, respectively. In the playoffs, Korkmaz made four starts in the [[2021 NBA playoffs#(1) Philadelphia 76ers vs. (5) Atlanta Hawks|2021 Eastern Conference semifinals]] against the [[2020–21 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]] when [[Danny Green (basketball)|Danny Green]] was injured, ending his season. On August 9, 2021, Korkmaz re-signed with the 76ers on a three-year contract.{{cite web|title=76ers Re-Sign Furkan Korkmaz|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-re-sign-furkan-korkmaz|website=NBA.com|date=August 9, 2021|access-date=August 10, 2021}} In February 2023, Korkmaz requested a trade from the 76ers for the second time during his stint with the team.{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Pompey|title=Sixers guard Furkan Korkmaz has requested to be traded before Thursday’s deadline, sources say|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sports/sixers-guard-furkan-korkmaz-nba-trade-deadline-20230206.html|work=The Inquirer|date=February 6, 2023|access-date=February 6, 2023}} On February 8, 2024, Korkmaz was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in a three-team deal involving the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Complete Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-complete-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}} and was waived the next day.{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Waive Furkan Korkmaz|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-waive-furkan-korkmaz|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}} ===AS Monaco (2024)=== On 7 August 2024, Korkmaz signed with [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]] of the [[LNB Élite]].{{cite web|title=FURKAN KORKMAZ, UN SNIPER DÉBARQUE À MONACO|url=https://asmonaco.basketball/news/show.php?ID=57829|website=ASMonaco.basketball|date=7 August 2024|access-date=7 August 2024|language=French}} In October 2024, Korkmaz suffered a slight tear in the right adductor and was expected to miss three to four weeks of action.{{cite web |title=Furkan Korkmaz out for three to four weeks |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1723580/furkan-korkmaz-out-for-three-to-four-weeks/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=11 October 2024 |language=en |date=5 October 2024}} ===Bahçeşehir Koleji (2025)=== On December 30, 2024, Korkmaz signed with [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=BKBasketbol |number=1873759654016127473 |title=Furkan Korkmaaz, Bahçeşehir Koleji'nde!}} ===Tofaş (2025–2026)=== On October 31, 2025, Korkmaz signed with [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://basketfaul.com.tr/turkiye/bsl/furkan-korkmaz-tofasta/|title=Furkan Korkmaz TOFAŞ’ta|date=October 31, 2025|website=|publisher=basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=October 31, 2025}} ===Beşiktaş (2026–present)=== On July 2, 2026, Korkmaz signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=BJK_Basketbol |number=2072720789791482200 |title=Resmi Açıklama Furkan Korkmaz}} ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== Korkmaz was a member of the junior national teams of Turkey. With Turkey's junior national teams, he played at: the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], which he led in scoring,{{Cite web |title=POINTS PER GAME : ALL ROUNDS |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/statistics/p/pid/100835/sid/9441/tid/376/_/2013_U16_European_Championship_Men_DIVISION_A/player-leaders.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425115936/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/statistics/p/pid/100835/sid/9441/tid/376/_/2013_U16_European_Championship_Men_DIVISION_A/player-leaders.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 25, 2018 |access-date=August 8, 2023 |website=archive.fiba.com}} the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where he won a gold medal, the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where he won a silver medal and was named to the All-Tournament Team, and at the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], where he won a bronze medal and was named to [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup All-Tournament Team|the All-Tournament Team]]. He also played at the [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], where he averaged 30.8 points, 10.6 rebounds, 10.8 assists, 8.6 steals, and 2.2 blocks per game, in 30.3 minutes per game. At the 2017 Under-20 tournament, he also shot 35.6% overall from the field, 27.6% from three-point range, and 66.7% from free throw range.{{Cite web |title=Furkan KORKMAZ STATISTICS |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2017/player/Furkan-Korkmaz |access-date=August 8, 2023 |website=fiba.basketball}} ===Senior national team=== Korkmaz played with the senior men's [[Turkey national basketball team|Turkish national basketball team]] at the [[EuroBasket 2015]], and at the [[2016 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament – Manila|2016 Manila FIBA World Olympic Qualifying
